answers.core:
With the addition of `GDExtensions`, I think it may be conceivable *for the most part* to do it (the `TypeServer` singleton, the many `TypeOperator` variations, the `TypeHandle` abstraction). However...

1. You wouldn't be able to have the property hint which would somewhat complicate the implementation of the necessary `EditorInspectorPlugin` code.
2. You would have to write the `DirectoryMonitor` logic yourself, effectively maintaining a duplicate of the `EditorFileSystem` class's functionality in two places. You then also run the risk of accidentally instantiating **two** objects that continuously watch, process, and cache data about all resource files in the project (not ideal).
answers.workaround: A long time ago, I once made a very poor attempt at implementing something like this. It was [nearly a thousand lines of code](https://github.com/godot-extended-libraries/godot-next/blob/master/addons/godot-next/references/class_type.gd) and very messy. And that doesn't even include any of the logic you'd need for a corresponding `EditorInspectorPlugin` to hack your way to a decent UI with it. It also didn't account for the flexibility of segregating the implementations of handling type operations.

title: Add improved abstractions for collecting, caching, and handling type information.
